# Proactive Support

`customer_support.model.proactive_support` · model · parent `—`

> We contact the customer before they contact us. That is the inversion of the entire domain: every other branch begins with a contact, a stated problem and implicit permission to reply, and this one begins with none of the three. There is no ticket, no question, no consent and no waiting customer — only a detection, an assumption about what it means to somebody, and a decision to interrupt them. . The characteristic failure is being indistinguishable from marketing, and it is not a tone problem. It is what the message actually is when the detection was wrong. If we contact someone about a problem they were going to contact us about, we are support and the value is enormous: we saved them the discovery, the frustration and the ticket. If we contact them about a problem they do not have, or would not have noticed, or had already worked around, then we are a vendor sending unsolicited mail about our own product — which is marketing, arriving in a channel the customer trusted for a different reason, and spending credibility that belongs to the whole company rather than to this programme. . That credibility is a shared, exhaustible budget and nobody owns it. The same inbox receives the release notes, the upsell, the survey and the outage notification, and support's ability to be believed during a genuine incident is drawn from the same account as a well-meaning proactive nudge about an expiring API key. Three teams contacting the same customer in one week is this branch's signature failure, and it is nobody's fault individually because no individual can see the other two. . The precision requirement is inverted relative to reactive support, and this is the part operators consistently underestimate. A reactive false positive is cheap: we ask a clarifying question and the customer corrects us in one line. A proactive false positive is expensive and invisible — nobody writes back to say "that did not apply to me", they simply read the next one less carefully, and the decay shows up nowhere until an important message goes unread. The threshold for firing has to be far higher than anything a reactive branch would tolerate, and the instinct to widen it once the programme needs numbers is what kills it. . Timing is a narrow window with a failure on each side. Too early and the customer had not noticed, so we have introduced a problem into their week and created the contact we claimed to prevent. Too late and we are apologising, which is reactive support with worse optics — the customer already knows, and now also knows we knew. . Measurement is counterfactual and therefore permanently contestable. Success is a contact that never happened, which cannot be observed and can only be estimated against a control group most organisations will not maintain because withholding help feels wrong. This makes the branch uniquely easy to claim victory in and uniquely hard to defend at budget time, and both of those are true simultaneously. . What an operator carries over wrongly from a reactive queue: assuming a reply path is free. A proactive message with no reply path is a broadcast and will be treated as one. A proactive message with a reply path generates inbound — often more inbound than it prevents, because it reminds people of adjacent things they had been living with. That can be an excellent trade if the contacts are cheaper and better-timed, but it is not the trade that was described to finance, and discovering it in month two is how the programme gets cancelled.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | nobody — there is no requester in this motion, which is the branch's defining property; the recipient is a customer selected by us who has asked for nothing |
| typical_resolution_hours | 0 |
| volume_shape | entirely supply-driven and self-set — volume is whatever the trigger population and contact-frequency budget allow, and it does not respond to demand at all |
| staffing_model | a small programme team owning triggers, content and frequency, with the reactive queue absorbing every reply the outreach generates |
| coverage | send-window rather than coverage — messages must land at a defensible local hour and the reply must be catchable when it arrives, which usually constrains sending more than the trigger does |
| automation_level | very high on selection and sending, and necessarily human on anything the customer sends back |
| primary_channels | `email`, `in_app`, `chat`, `phone` |
| notes | The reply is where this branch ends. The moment a customer responds, the contact leaves this motion and re-enters the reactive one, carrying context the reactive queue did not generate and usually cannot see — the agent receives a reply to a message they did not send about a detection they cannot inspect. That handover is where proactive programmes actually die, far more often than at the targeting step everyone worries about.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`

Requires `read_confidence_bp`, `measured_on`, `attributed_to`, `sample_size_messages`


> Silence after outbound is the dominant response and it is unreadable. It is not consent, not satisfaction and not indifference — it is the absence of a reason to reply to something nobody asked for. The canonical read treats no-response as weakly neutral, which is defensible when we owe someone an answer and indefensible here, so read_confidence on any sentiment inferred from a proactive thread should be substantially lower than the same inference on a reactive one, and `sample_size_messages` is usually one.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.commitment`

Requires `due_at`, `state`, `breach_was_silent`


> Proactive messages contain promises nobody asked for — "we will let you know when this is fixed", "we are monitoring it and will follow up on Friday" — and they are promises in exactly the way a promise made in a ticket is. They are also the ones most reliably forgotten, because there is no open ticket ageing on a board to remind anyone. An unfulfilled proactive commitment is worse than never having written, since it converted a gesture of competence into evidence of the opposite.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`

Requires `preferred_channel`, `timezone`, `working_hours`, `language`


> Outbound without permission has to be defensible on every axis that is available: the right channel, a reasonable local hour, the language they use with us. None of this makes an unwanted message wanted, but each of them is a way of making a wanted message land as support rather than as a campaign, and getting the hour wrong is enough on its own to move a message from one category to the other.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `created_at`, `channel`, `requester_ref`


> A ticket opened by us is not a demand signal, and any volume series that mixes self-opened contacts with customer-raised ones is corrupted at the source — the branch will appear to increase support demand while reducing it. Keep the two populations separable at creation; it cannot be reconstructed afterwards, and every analysis this branch is judged on depends on the distinction.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article`

Requires `intent_covered`, `findability`, `last_verified_at`


> Every proactive message should point at a durable version of its own explanation. Without one, the same reasoning is rewritten into each send, drifts between them, cannot be corrected once sent, and leaves the customer nowhere to go when they return to it three weeks later — which is the point at which they most want to reread it.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.churn_risk`

Requires `confidence_bp`, `primary_driver`, `driver_evidence`


> This branch is where churn risk stops being a report and becomes a trigger for contacting a specific person, which is a much higher bar. A risk score good enough to rank accounts for a QBR is not good enough to justify an unsolicited message, because the cost of being wrong is paid in the relationship being scored rather than in a slide.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **experimental**


> This is the branch the current substrate starves most completely. Everything it runs on is a detection — usage falling away, an error rate rising for one tenant, an expiry approaching, a known defect matched to the customers exposed to it — and Layer 1 and 2 emit none of those today. What the engine can see is a thread and a promise, which supports exactly one honest proactive motion: following up on something we already said we would do. That is a narrow branch of this branch, it is genuinely valuable, and it is the only part of this file that can run before a support pack ships.
